Description: Specifies the mode by which MS2 and MS3 ions are generated
Valid Values: CID, ETD, EThcD, HCD, not applicable

Description: Collision-induced dissociation (CID); a fragmentation method in which peptide ions are activated by collision with neutral gas molecules, generating b- and y-type fragment ions primarily from peptide backbone cleavage

Electron transfer dissociation (ETD); a fragmentation method in which electrons are transferred to multiply-charged peptide cations, generating c- and z-type fragment ions particularly suited for analysis of post-translational modifications

Electron transfer/higher-energy collision dissociation (EThcD); a hybrid fragmentation method combining ETD and HCD to generate both c/z-type and b/y-type fragment ions, providing complementary sequence coverage especially for phosphopeptide analysis

Higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD); an Orbitrap-based fragmentation method that produces b- and y-type fragment ions with higher energy than CID, enabling high-resolution and high-mass-accuracy MS2 spectra
Indicates that fragmentation was not used.
